    Rays of the fibres of the zero-product family #

    Proposition 11.3(3) (binary-families.tex), in the form used by Proposition 7.9: let B be an algebra with a linear isomorphism Ψ : kP → B carrying a fibre product m_c = m + Σ c_z ε_z to the product of B. "Corrections involve only generating nonlocal inputs. Products with local basis vectors […] are unchanged. Thus the local rings and both endpoint actions are the same as in A₀, and the basis vectors represent exactly the same endpoint-unit orbits." Hence the images Ψ b_e are a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents of B, and the images Ψ b_r are a ray transversal. When the coefficients are zero or one, products of these vectors are basis vectors or zero, and by Corollary 3.3 the transversal is a normed multiplicative basis.

    Deviation: the fibre is not formed as a separate algebra; everything is read in B through Ψ, which is how Proposition 7.9 uses it.

    Corrections vanish on local inputs #

                  Endpoint subbimodules of a fibre are spanned by rays #

                  The endpoint actions of the fibre are those of kP (Ψ_mul_left, Ψ_mul_right), so an endpoint subbimodule of B pulls back to one of kP, which is spanned by rays since kP is representation-finite. No representation-finiteness of B is needed.
